title: On‑Prem Audit Proxy + Approval Lattice PRD (draft)
content:
Context / problem
- Customers deploying Redwood Private (on‑prem/VPC) require low-latency, tamper-evident audit capture for network and control-plane events, combined with flexible approval gates so their operators can sign/authorize changes without routing all traffic through Redwood control plane.
- Existing PRDs focus on evidence retention and attestation bundles; this draft explores an 'audit proxy' appliance + local approval lattice that: 1) interposes with minimal added latency, 2) emits compact cryptographic proof bundles, and 3) supports multi-party approval policies for network-change operations.

High level proposal
- Ship a lightweight on‑prem Audit Proxy binary (container or small VM image) that sits in customer control plane (adjacent to e.g. edge orchestrator) and acts as:
  - Ingress tap for change operations (VPC peering connect/disconnect, route updates, firewall policy changes, certificate rotations)
  - Local policy evaluator that enforces approval lattice (k-of-n, role‑based escalation, time‑outs)
  - Compact evidence emitter: signs an immutable event record and pushes to customer long‑term store (S3/GCS/remote syslog) + optional hashed anchor to Redwood control plane for cross‑tenant correlation (only when customer opts in)

Goals (what success looks like)
- Latency: additional median add-to-commit latency <= 6ms for simple approvals when proxy runs in same AZ as operator tooling (goal 3ms).
- Tamper evidence: every recorded event must be cryptographically signed by the proxy and include a monotonic sequence and a verifiable commit proof.
- Flexibility: support operator-configurable approval lattice policies (examples below) plus a safe default allowlist.
- Usability: customers can onboard with 2 CLI commands and one YAML to describe approvals for first 5 network resources.
- Auditability: Redwood Console (when connected) can show a read‑only view of the on‑prem evidence timeline and highlight missing proofs or gaps.

Non‑goals
- This doc does not specify full HSM integration (HSM/KMS integration is follow-up).
- Not building distributed consensus between proxies (single proxy per site is MVP).

User personas / primary flows
- Network Operator (on‑prem) creates a firewall rule change via operator UI/CLI -> proxy intercepts, checks policy, either allows and records or blocks and generates a pending approval ticket. If pending, the operator receives an approval URL (or CLI token) to escalate.
- Security Reviewer remotely queries evidence store for changes in last 90 days; proxy provides signed event bundles for the requested time window.
- SRE on Redwood side receives optional anchored hashes and uses them for correlation in high‑severity incident postmortems (only if customer opted in).

Approval lattice examples (policy DSL sketches)
- Simple: approvers: [net-ops-lead], k:1, timeout: 30m, auto_reject_on_timeout: false
- Escalation: stage1 approvers: [devops], stage2 approvers: [sec-ops, infra-lead], k:1 per stage, escalation_after: 15m
- Multi‑party: approvers: [cust-acct-owner, cust-legal], k:2, require_presence: true (means physical presence or MFA step)
- Conditional: if resource=="internet-egress" then approvers: [sec-ops], k:1, audit_level: "high"

Event record sketch (compact JSON string saved and signed)
- fields: [event_id, ts_iso, local_seq, actor, actor_auth_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, diff_summary, policy_id, approvals: [ {approver, ts, decision, signature}], proxy_sig, prev_hash, anchor_hash_optional]
- Stored as line‑delimited JSON with binary detached signature (or in a small sqlite WAL for high‑throughput scenarios).

Sampling and retention strategy (for telemetry & audit exports)
- Full fidelity: all approval decisions and resulting commit events must be retained at customer-chosen retention window.
- Sampled telemetry: for broader telemetry (latency, gate hit rates), proxy emits aggregated metrics every 10s with a sliding 1m window.
- Adaptive sampling: if gate hit rate > 5% (unexpected), switch to 100% capture for 1 hour to aid debugging.

Operator UX (local)
- CLI: redwood-proxy approve --action id=evt_123 --approver me --mfa=otp -> returns signed approval token
- Web: small local web UI that lists pending approvals, with reason, time-to-expire, and one-click escalate (opens mail-to configured approvers).
- Notification: support webhook, email, and Slack (customer configured) for pending approvals.

APIs between components (sketches)
- Proxy REST (local-only bind): POST /events -> returns {status, event_id, need_approval: bool, approval_url}
- POST /approvals/{event_id} -> body {approver_id, method, token} -> returns signed approval envelope
- GET /export?from=ts&to=ts&format=ndjson -> stream of signed event records

Security & compliance notes
- Proxy signs with a site key; private key can live in customer KMS or locally protected keystore. Public key registered with Redwood only if anchoring is enabled.
- Replay protection via local_seq + prev_hash chain and optional monotonic counter.
- Tamper detection: missing sequence numbers or broken prev_hash => flag as possible tamper, surface in evidence summary.
- Regulatory retention: customers can set retention windows per resource type; proxy supports scripted legal-hold to prevent pruning.

Performance considerations and mitigations
- Minimal synchronous crypto: sign only compact hash of record; bulk-signing in batches for high QPS endpoints; immediate local append then async sign for non-blocking commits (configurable trade-off: latency vs absolute proof at write).
- Fast path for allowlist changes: small allowlist in memory so common operations skip policy engine.

Deployment / rollout plan (MVP -> v1 -> enterprise)
- MVP (Q1): single-proxy container, local filesystem evidence store, YAML policies, local CLI/web UI, ndjson export. Focus: correctness and latency measurements.
- v1 (Q2): KMS integrations, secure upgrade path, SQLite WAL option, aggregated telemetry, Redwood optional anchor service.
- Enterprise (Q3): HSM support, multi‑proxy sync, cross-site evidence merging, RBAC sync with SSO (SCIM).

Monitoring & SLOs
- Proxy health: uptime 99.9% (per site).
- Approval latency SLO:  p50 < 6ms, p95 < 40ms (depends on policy complexity).
- Evidence export throughput: support 1000 events/sec on commodity 4vCPU/8GB box in MVP mode.

Open questions / risks
- Legal: what counts as 'signed evidence' for customer auditors in regulated industries? Need legal + compliance input.
- UX: how to present approvals to reduce accidental approvals while keeping MTTR low?
- Key management: preferred customer-hosted patterns (bring-your-own-kms vs local sealed key) and backup/rotation UX.
- Anchoring: privacy concerns if customers want to anchor hashes to Redwood control plane—define opt-in contract and minimal metadata.

Next steps (immediate)
- Engineering spike: build a minimal proxy that accepts POST /events, appends to NDJSON, signs with ephemeral key, and returns event_id. Owner: Miguel. (2w)
- Security review: draft threat model for proxy and key lifecycle. Owner: Priya. (1w)
- UX workshop: sketch local web UI and CLI flows, validate with two pilot customers. Owner: Ben. (2w)

Notes to self / rough ideas (working draft tone)
- Think about "evidence delta" packing to reduce export volume (e.g., store diffs + occasional full snapshot)
- Consider offline mode (store events when no outbound connectivity; anchor queue when reconnect)
- Potentially reuse parts of the existing telemetry agent codebase to avoid new amplification of maintenance burden

References / related items
- Acceptance criteria will be written as Linear tickets (RDW-49xx) and linked in PRD before handoff.
- See sketch: https://figma.redwood.ai/proxy-audit-ui (internal)

Draft ends — feedback wanted on policy DSL tradeoffs and acceptable latency guardrails.
